channel.title: Debt Payoff & Budgeting
channel.description: Free debt, budget, and savings calculators, plus Excel templates.

item.title: Credit Card Payoff Calculator: How Long Will It Take?
item.description: Paying only the minimum on a $5,000 card at 22% APR takes over 19 years and costs about $8,100 in interest. A fixed $250 a month clears it in 26 months. See your own payoff date and interest, free, no sign-up.

item.title: Debt Snowball vs Avalanche Calculator (Free)
item.description: Snowball pays the smallest balance first; avalanche pays the highest interest rate first. Enter your own debts to see your debt-free date, total interest, and payoff order under both methods. Free, no sign-up, nothing leaves your browser.

item.title: Loan Calculator With Extra Payments (Free)
item.description: On a $25,000 car loan at 7% for 60 months, paying $100 extra a month pays it off 11 months early and saves $938.99 in interest. Try your own loan, extra payments, or a lump sum, with a full amortization schedule.

item.title: Debt Payoff Calculator: See Your Debt-Free Date
item.description: Keep paying the same total each month and roll each paid-off debt's payment into the next one. In this example, $200 extra a month gets you debt-free 20 months sooner and saves $3,554 in interest. Free calculator, snowball or avalanche.

item.title: Savings Goal Calculator: How Long to Save $10,000
item.description: At 4% APY, saving $300 a month reaches $10,000 in 32 months; $500 a month gets there in 20. Enter your goal, what you have, and your rate to see your date or the monthly amount you need. Free, no sign-up.

item.title: 50/30/20 Budget Calculator (Free)
item.description: The 50/30/20 rule splits take-home pay into needs, wants, and savings. On $4,000 a month that's $2,000, $1,200, and $800. Enter your own pay and, if you like, what you spend now to see where you stand.

item.title: Loan Calculator: 36 vs 48 vs 60 Month Loan Interest
item.description: On a $20,000 loan at 8%, stretching from 36 to 60 months drops the payment from $626.73 to $405.53 a month but raises total interest from $2,562.18 to $4,331.67. See your payment, interest, and what extra payments save. Free, no sign-up.

item.title: Debt Payoff Planner Spreadsheet: Snowball + Avalanche (Excel)
item.description: Enter your debts once and get a month-by-month plan for both the snowball and avalanche methods, your debt-free date, total interest, payoff order, and a payment log to track your real progress.

item.title: Monthly Budget Spreadsheet: Zero-Based + 50/30/20 (Excel)
item.description: Plan every dollar at the start of the month, log what you spend, and see planned vs actual for each category, every month, plus a year summary with an income vs spending chart.
